# Batch mode

<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

Batch mode provides asynchronous transcription for large or complex jobs that require processing multiple files or lengthy recordings.

## Capabilities

-   Parallel file processing
-   Asynchronous operation
-   Large-scale recording support
-   Multi-speaker and multi-channel audio support
-   Language detection, model selection, custom vocabulary, and Text Polishing (`en-US` only, without language detection)

Each audio file generates its own transcript that saves to a corresponding output location.

## How it works

Batch mode processing runs asynchronously and enables you to transcribe multiple files in a single API call.

This mode is ideal for workflows that involve large file collections.

## Input

The API supports three input modes.

| Mode       | Description                                                                                      |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `SINGLE`   | A single audio file. Inferred when the URI points to a single file.                              |
| `PREFIX`   | All files under a shared S3 prefix/container. Supports glob filters to include or exclude files. |
| `MANIFEST` | An explicit list of file URIs. Maximum 1,000 files per manifest.                                 |

## Output

The API supports three output layouts.

| Layout     | Description                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SINGLE`   | Use the output URI as a single transcript file path. Valid only with `SINGLE` input. The `uri` can be a pre-signed HTTPS URL, in which case `auth` isn't needed. |
| `ADJACENT` | Place each transcript next to its input file (same directory). Valid only with `PREFIX` input. No output `uri` is needed, but `destination` is required.         |
| `PREFIX`   | Use the output URI as the base directory for all transcripts. Required for `MANIFEST` input.                                                                     |

With `PREFIX` and `ADJACENT` layouts, each transcript is named after its input file with a unique suffix, such as `a1.wav_8931d872-85bd-4fdf-b133-822c4090e008.json`. With the `SINGLE` layout, the transcript is written to the exact output `uri`.

## Audio requirements

-   Formats: WAV, MP3, M4A, MP4, and WebM
-   Channels: Mono or stereo
-   Sample rate: At least 8 kHz; 16 kHz or greater is recommended
-   Maximum duration per file: 2 hours
-   Maximum size per file: 300 MB

## Transcription options

These options control recognition. For full descriptions, see [Speech configuration](/docs/ai-services/scribe/speech-configuration/).

| Parameter            | Type    | Default   | Description                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------- | ------- | --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `language`           | string  | `en-US`   | Language code, such as `en-US`. See [Speech configuration](/docs/ai-services/scribe/speech-configuration/) for supported languages.     |
| `segmentation_mode`  | string  | `"auto"`  | Voice Activity Detection (VAD) mode. Set `"none"` to disable.                                                                           |
| `word_time_offsets`  | boolean | `false`   | Include word-level timestamps.                                                                                                          |
| `channel_separation` | boolean | `false`   | Transcribe stereo channels separately.                                                                                                  |
| `diarization`        | boolean | `false`   | Identify speakers and add a speaker tag to each transcript segment.                                                                     |
| `model`              | string  | Automatic | Select a compatible recognition model.                                                                                                  |
| `language_detection` | object  | —         | Detect each file's language once or continuously. Omit `model` when `mode` is `once`.                                                   |
| `profanity_filter`   | boolean | `false`   | Filter profanity when supported by the selected model.                                                                                  |
| `text_polishing`     | object  | —         | Whether to return polished text. `enabled` boolean defaults to `false`. See [Text Polishing](/docs/ai-services/scribe/text-polishing/). |
| `vocabulary`         | object  | —         | Apply an inline phrase list to every file in the job.                                                                                   |
| `vocabulary_id`      | string  | —         | Apply a persistent Vocabulary Asset.                                                                                                    |

For model and language options, see [Speech configuration](/docs/ai-services/scribe/speech-configuration/). For vocabulary options, see [Custom vocabulary](/docs/ai-services/scribe/custom-vocabulary/).

## Batch jobs

### Create a batch job

To create a new batch transcription job, use this endpoint:

**`POST /aiservices/scribe/jobs`**

You can optionally include a `reference_id` for tracking.

To receive webhook notifications when a job finishes, include a `notifications` object with a `webhook_url` and a `secret` for payload verification.

#### Example request (cURL)

This cURL example submits a batch transcription job from S3 and defines the output location and settings. The response returns a job ID and status so you can track processing.

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.zoom.us/v2/aiservices/scribe/jobs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "input": {
      "mode": "PREFIX",
      "source": "S3",
      "uri": "s3://acme-bucket/audio/2026/10/",
      "filters": {
        "include_globs": ["**/*.wav", "**/*.mp3"],
        "exclude_globs": ["**/tmp/**"]
      },
      "auth": {
        "aws": {
          "access_key_id": "AKIA...",
          "secret_access_key": "wJalrX...",
          "session_token": "FwoGZXIvYXdzE..."
        }
      }
    },
    "output": {
      "destination": "S3",
      "uri": "s3://acme-bucket/transcripts/2026/10/",
      "layout": "PREFIX",
      "auth": {
        "aws": {
          "access_key_id": "AKIA...",
          "secret_access_key": "wJalrX...",
          "session_token": "FwoGZXIvYXdzE..."
        }
      }
    },
    "config": {
      "language": "en-US",
      "model": "zoom-scribe-en",
      "word_time_offsets": true,
      "channel_separation": false,
      "diarization": false
    },
    "outputs": {
      "text_polishing": {
        "enabled": true
      }
    },
    "notifications": {
      "webhook_url": "https://example.com/hooks/scribe",
      "secret": "hmac-secret"
    },
    "reference_id": "import-2025-11"
  }'
```

Use temporary AWS STS credentials in `auth.aws`, including `session_token`.

Each completed output file contains the original transcript. When Text Polishing is enabled, the file also contains `outputs.text_polishing.text`. See [Text Polishing](/docs/ai-services/scribe/text-polishing/).

#### Response (201)

```json
{
    "job_id": "8e5a1f3c-2d7b-4c9e-a6f1-0b4d7e2c9a58",
    "state": "QUEUED",
    "submitted_at": "2026-01-05T18:34:12Z"
}
```

### Batch job endpoints

Five additional endpoints are available to manage batch jobs.

| Action               | Description                                                      | Endpoint                                                                      |
| -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Get batch job status | Check the current status and progress summary of a specific job. | `GET /aiservices/scribe/jobs/{jobId}`                                         |
| List batch jobs      | View all batch jobs, optionally filtered by state.               | `GET /aiservices/scribe/jobs?state=QUEUED&page_size=50&next_page_token=...`   |
| Cancel batch job     | Cancel a job that is in `QUEUED` or `PROCESSING` state.          | `DELETE /aiservices/scribe/jobs/{jobId}`                                      |
| List batch job files | Retrieve per-file status with pagination.                        | `GET /aiservices/scribe/jobs/{jobId}/files?page_size=200&next_page_token=...` |
| Get batch job file   | Retrieve the status and output location of an individual file.   | `GET /aiservices/scribe/jobs/{jobId}/files/{fileId}`                          |

List responses include a `next_cursor` field. Pass its value as the `next_page_token` query parameter to retrieve the next page.

### Job and file states

Files in a job are processed independently. If any file fails or is skipped while others succeed, the job ends in `PARTIAL`. The job status response includes a `summary` with counts for `total_files`, `queued`, `processing`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `canceled`.

| Job state    | Description                                                   |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `QUEUED`     | The job is waiting to start.                                  |
| `PROCESSING` | Files are being transcribed.                                  |
| `SUCCEEDED`  | All files were transcribed.                                   |
| `PARTIAL`    | Some files were transcribed, and some failed or were skipped. |
| `FAILED`     | The job failed.                                               |
| `CANCELED`   | The job was canceled. This is a terminal state.               |

| File state        | Description                                                                                                 |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `FILE_QUEUED`     | The file is waiting to be processed.                                                                        |
| `FILE_PROCESSING` | The file is being transcribed.                                                                              |
| `FILE_SUCCEEDED`  | The transcript was written to the output location.                                                          |
| `FILE_FAILED`     | The file couldn't be transcribed.                                                                           |
| `FILE_CANCELED`   | Processing was canceled for the file.                                                                       |
| `FILE_SKIPPED`    | The file was skipped because its extension isn't supported. The file's `error.code` is `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA`. |

### Webhook verification

When you provide a `secret` in the `notifications` object, the API signs each webhook request so you can verify that Zoom AI Services sent it.

Each webhook request includes two headers.

| Header                   | Description                                                   |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `x-zm-signature`         | HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request, prefixed with `sha256=` |
| `x-zm-request-timestamp` | Unix timestamp of when the request was sent                   |

To verify the signature:

1. Compute the `HMAC-SHA256` of the string `v0:{timestamp}:{raw_body}` using your secret key
2. Compare it with the value in `x-zm-signature` using a timing-safe comparison to prevent timing attacks.
3. Reject the request if the signatures do not match or if the timestamp is stale.

```javascript
const message = `v0:${timestamp}:${rawBody}`;
const expected = `sha256=${crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret).update(message).digest("hex")}`;
const a = Buffer.from(signature);
const b = Buffer.from(expected);
const isValid = a.length === b.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(a, b);
```
